newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices stabilise, sentiment cautious.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices stabilise, sentiment cautious.

text.p: China's stock indices stabilised on Monday after sharp losses last Friday due to Beijing's ban on state banks trading on the stock markets, but market sentiment remained cautious, traders said.
Shanghai's B share index closed up on a technical rebound, gaining 0.811 points or 0.95 percent to 86.148 on thin volume of 8.7 million shares worth $6.1 million.

The index lost 4.34 percent last Friday after the People's Bank of China, the central bank, ordered state banks to offset their existing stock positions within 10 days and stop trading on the state debt repurchase and spot market immediately.

Shanghai's A share index ended slightly down on cautious sentiment after the recent official crackdown on the stock markets and amid market talk that further measures would be introduced to cool down trading, traders said.
The index lost 0.769 points or 0.06 percent to 1,331.168 on volume of 327.3 million shares worth 4.7 billion yuan.
In Shenzhen, the A share index rose 5.44 points or 1.24 percent to end at 445.65 on turnover of 7.2 billion yuan against Friday's 12.7 billion yuan on bargain-hunting, traders said.
There was no trading on Shenzhen's foreign currency B share market on Monday due to a public holiday in Hong Kong, the Dragon Boat Festival. Trading will resume on Tuesday.
"The day's rise (on the Shanghai B share market) was mainly due to a technical rebound," said a trader. "Market sentiment was cautious after Friday's falls, making trading volume very thin."
"Today's rebound was spurred by small investors who anticipated quick profits," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Despite the rally, the market's outlook remains gloomy as banks, which used to be the major institutional investors, pull out of the market, Shenzhen analysts said.
"The ban has drained some of the market's liquidity and I expect turnover to dwindle this week as investors take a wait-and-see attitude," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The ban will effectively cut off the main source of "hot money" (speculative funds) from the markets, brokers said.
On the Shanghai B share market, bicycle maker Shanghai Phoenix Co was the star performer on a technical rebound, jumping $0.012 or 9.37 percent to $0.140 on volume of 100,000 shares.
In Shenzhen, Shanxi Zhangze Electric Power Co Ltd, which debuted in Shenzhen with a flotation of 40 million A shares, closed at 16.98 yuan against an issue price of 6.00 yuan per share.
